title: Update Directional Light Shadows to Work with Asymmetrical Cameras

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
Switched from 'set_prespective' inside _light_instance_setup_directional_shadow which assumes a symmetrical camera frustum to get_endpoints which takes into account any camera frustum offsets. Also updated the orthogonal code to utilize get_endpoints to take advantage of some math I already had to do and to keep them utilizing the same code path so to speak. This change fixes both shadow placement and shadow culling for camera's with an asymmetrical frustum.

Video showing it working:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d7ed986-bd8f-471f-9e95-8cf710a85b5d

AI (Claude specifically) was used to help determine where the issue lied (in renderer_scene_cull.cpp) and then in what function (_light_instance_setup_directional_shadow) as I am still learning engine source. AI was also used to help generate a solution (utilizing get_endpoints). Edits to this solution and comments on it were done by me. 

## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Closes #123399 

## Additional information

I have not run any unit tests on these changes (I'm still not sure how to do that to be honest... This is my first contribution). But I did confirm manually in my test scene that Perspective and Orthogonal projections still behaved as expected. As long as my math checks out to other people, I believe this PR to be relatively straightforward. With that being said, I did not run any XR tests. I don't image there to be any issues there, but I did want to bring up that XR is an untested area.
